structured.answer: I'd use option C, the S&P 500 group with the return and fund size columns. In it I'd lean to the Phoenix S&P track: about 12% a year over 5 years, 3.4 billion ₪ in it, and a name I know.

stuck.where: Option A, the long list of rows
stuck.why: Every row looks the same: 0.5-something % fee, 99%/99% and a ring. After about 20 rows I couldn't tell any of them apart, and I nearly closed it.

stuck.where: Two fee numbers per row, מהחיסכון and מההפקדות
stuck.why: I didn't know which one actually costs me or how much in shekels. I just looked at the first one.

stuck.where: Option B mixes everything in one list
stuck.why: A bond track sits next to an S&P track sorted by fee, so the cheapest row at the top (עוקב מדדים גמיש with 55% מניות) looked like the one to take, but it isn't what I came for.

stuck.where: Rows in C that say פחות מ־3 שנים instead of a return
stuck.why: Is that bad or just new? I skipped those funds.

findings.what: A has no return and no size, so every S&P row looks the same and I can't choose. I'd have gone back.
The fees are only small percents, never shekels, so the 0.52 vs 0.71 difference feels like nothing
The list is way too long on a phone: dozens of near-identical rows
B puts bond and mixed tracks on top just because they're cheap, which is misleading if you want the S&P
Two fee lines per row, and nothing says which one matters
Lots of rows have no return (פחות מ־3 שנים), which makes them look suspicious
The recommended badge is on A, but A tells me the least
Small names like אינפיניטי, אנליסט and איילון sit next to the big ones without telling me who they are
